items.claim_text: # We Thought It Was AI—But There Was a Person Inside Meta’s Muse
Ring, ring.
A call seemed to come from an AI agent.
But as the conversation went on, the voice was not AI at all.
It was a person.
Meta had run a test that caused exactly this surprise.
It was like someone took off an AI costume.
Then a person stepped out.
Having a person take over is not always a bad thing.
A human can handle situations that AI alone finds difficult.
As a system, this may even be useful.
But this was where the problem began.
It is one thing to speak because you think a machine is listening.
It is another when you know a person is listening.
When people share their names, plans, or personal situations, it matters who listens.
### The hidden person behind the AI sign
Here was the reveal.
The test began without clearly telling users that contract workers would make the calls.
A user might think the exchange was with AI, even though a person was involved.
AI had not learned to speak like a human.
A human stood behind the sign that said AI.
It seemed like a story from the future.
But the main question was very basic: Had users been clearly told who was making the call?
As AI becomes able to make calls or reservations for us, this question will become more familiar.
The more useful the feature, the more people will want to know who is on the other side.
They will want to know if it is AI or human.
The test had begun without clearly telling users.
In the AI age, technology that makes a voice sound human is not enough.
We must also know, at the start, who is on the other end.
Before AI speaks for us, we need to know whether the voice belongs to AI or a person.

C17.reason: 「ここが明かされた点だ」という修辞的なつなぎである。
